blurb: '47 is an American lifestyle brand that brings together sports, fashion, and cultural influences. It offers a wide range of licensed headwear, apparel and gear tailored for men, women, and children. The brand has been owned by New Era Cap Company since August 2024.

title: 11.11 / eleven eleven
about: Slow-made clothing with artisans across India
blurb: A designer label making small batches of slow-made clothing with groups of artisans across India, working with indigenous fibres such as Ponduru red cotton.

title: Abercrombie & Fitch
blurb: Abercrombie & Fitch Co. is an American lifestyle retailer founded in 1892, which focuses on contemporary clothing targeting customers in their early 20s to mid 40s.

title: Abraham & Thakore
blurb: Luxury Indian fashion that blends handloom textiles with modern minimalism: kurtas, saris, shirts and accessories.

title: Angarkha
about: Traditional upper garment in India subcontinent
blurb: Angarkha is an outer robe with long sleeves which was worn by men in Indian subcontinent. By the 19th-century it had become the generally accepted attire of an educated man in public.

title: Antariya
blurb: An Antariya is a lower body garment from ancient India. It is a long white or coloured strip of cotton passed through the legs, tucked at the back and covering the legs loosely, then flowing into long pleats at front of the legs.

title: Aran jumper
blurb: A thick cream wool sweater from Ireland's Aran Islands, covered in cable stitches said to bring fishermen luck.

title: Arani Silk Sarees
about: Traditional sari made in Arani, Tamil Nadu, India
blurb: Arani Silk Sarees are traditional silk sarees made in the town of Arani, located in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. Because these sarees are produced in Arani, the town is often referred to as the Silk City of Arani or Arani Silk City.

title: Baluchari sari
blurb: Baluchari Sari is a type of sari, a garment worn by women in the Indian states of West Bengal, Tripura and Assam and the country of Bangladesh. This particular type of sari originated in West Bengal and is known for depictions of mythological scenes on the anchal of the sari.

title: Banarasi sari
blurb: A Banarasi sari is a sari made in Varanasi, an ancient city in the Bhojpur-Purvanchal region, which is also called Benares. The saris are among the finest saris in India and are known for their gold and silver brocade or zari, fine silk and opulent embroidery.

title: Bomkai sari
blurb: Bomkai sari or Bomkai Saree is a handloom saree from Odisha, India. It is an origin of Bomkai village from Ganjam district, however later it is mainly produced by the Bhulia community of Subarnapur district. Bomkai is one of the identified Geographical Indications of India.

title: Buckskins
blurb: Buckskins are clothing, usually consisting of a jacket and leggings, made from buckskin, a soft sueded leather from the hide of deer.

title: Buffalo coat
blurb: A buffalo coat is a heavy winter garment made from the bison, which also commonly known as the "buffalo".

title: Buffalo robe
about: Buffalo hides used by Plains Indians
blurb: A buffalo robe is a cured buffalo pelt, with the hair left on. They are used as blankets, saddles, or as trade items by Plains Indians, the Native Americans from the vast grasslands of the Interior Plains.

title: Button blanket
about: Wool blanket embellished with mother-of-pearl buttons
blurb: A button blanket is wool blanket embellished with mother-of-pearl buttons, created by Northwest Coastal tribes, that is worn for ceremonial purposes. The blankets are used as capes and gifts at ceremonial dances and potlatches, and not used for sleeping.

title: Capote
blurb: A capote or capot is a long wrap-style wool coat with a hood. From the early days of the North American fur trade, both indigenous peoples and European Canadian settlers fashioned wool blankets into "capotes" as a means of coping with harsh winters.

title: Carhartt
blurb: Carhartt, Inc. is an American clothing company founded in 1889, known for heavy-duty work wear such as jackets, coats, overalls, coveralls, vests, shirts, jeans, dungarees, fire-resistant clothing and hunting apparel.

title: Chamba Rumal
blurb: The Chamba Rumal or Chamba handkerchief is an embroidered handicraft that was once promoted under the patronage of the former rulers of Chamba kingdom. It is a common gift during marriages with detailed patterns in bright colour schemes.

title: Chanderi sari
blurb: The Chanderi sari is a traditional silk sari made in Chanderi, Madhya Pradesh, India.

title: Chattayum mundum
blurb: Chattayum mundum is a traditional attire used by the Syrian Christian women of Kerala, India.

title: Chikankari
about: Traditional embroidery style from Lucknow, India
blurb: Chikankari is a traditional embroidery style from Lucknow, India. Translated, the word means embroidery, and it is one of Lucknow's best known textile decoration styles. The main market in Lucknow for Chikankari based products is Chowk.

title: Choli
about: Type of crop top worn with the sari
blurb: A choli or ravike is a blouse or a bodice-like upper garment, that is usually cut short or cropped leaving the midriff bare worn by women in the Indian subcontinent. It is also known as ravike in South India. It is worn along with a sari in the Indian subcontinent.

title: Christy Dawn
blurb: Christy Dawn makes clothing around a commitment to regeneration, building what it calls reciprocal relationships that heal community and the earth. Its store is in Los Angeles.

title: Chrome Hearts
blurb: Chrome Hearts is a luxury brand from Hollywood, Los Angeles, primarily producing silver, gold, and diamond accessories, alongside eyewear, leather items, apparel, furniture, kitchenware, and miscellaneous other items, using leather, silver, and ebony.

title: Columbia Sportswear
about: American company that manufactures and distributes outerwear and sportswear
blurb: The Columbia Sportswear Company is an American company that manufactures and distributes outerwear, sportswear, and footwear, as well as headgear, camping equipment, ski apparel, and outerwear accessories. It was founded in 1938 by Paul Lamfrom, the father of Gert Boyle.

title: Coonskin cap
about: Hat fashioned from the skin and fur of a raccoon
blurb: A coonskin cap is a hat fashioned from the skin and fur of a raccoon. The headwear became associated with European Americans occupying lands on the United States borders with Indigenous nations in the late 18th century and the first half of the 19th century.

title: Dehen 1920
about: Wool sweaters and outerwear from Portland, Oregon
blurb: A family-owned company that has made wool sweaters, shirts and outerwear in Portland, Oregon, since 1920.

title: Dharmavaram silk sari
blurb: Dharmavaram silk saris are textiles woven by hand with mulberry silk and zari. They are made in Dharmavaram of Sri Sathya Sai district in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. It was registered as one of the geographical indication from Andhra Pradesh by Geographical Indications of Goods Act, 1999.

title: Dhoti
about: Ethnic wrap garment worn by men in the Indian subcontinent
blurb: The dhoti is an ankle-length breechcloth, wrapped around the waist and the legs, in resemblance to the shape of trousers. The dhoti is a garment of ethnic wear for men in the Indian subcontinent.

title: Doodlage
blurb: An eco-fashion label making upcycled, recycled and zero-waste clothing, made to order with fair-wage production, from its studio in Delhi.

title: Dupatta
about: Cloth wrap worn as a shawl, scarf, or veil in the Indian Subcontinent
blurb: The dupattā, also called chunni, chunari, chundari, lugda, rao/rawo, gandhi, pothi, orna, and odhni is a long shawl-like scarf traditionally worn by both women and men in the Indian subcontinent.

title: Durumagi
about: Korean overcoat with no back or side vents
blurb: Durumagi is a variety of po, or overcoat, in hanbok, the traditional Korean attire. It is a form of outerwear that is usually worn as the topmost layer of clothing over a jeogori and baji.

title: Duster
blurb: A duster is a light, loose-fitting, long coat.

title: Freenote Cloth
about: Menswear cut, sewn and finished in California
blurb: Freenote makes a classic menswear collection manufactured only in the United States; every piece is cut, sewn and finished in California.

title: Galloon
about: Decorated woven or braided fabric trim
blurb: Galloon is a heavily-decorated woven or braided trim, typically made of, or featuring, gold or silver thread, which may be woven or embroidered. Galloon trim is used in the trim of military and police uniforms, ecclesiastical dress, and as trim on textiles, drapery, and upholstery.

title: Gamosa
about: Woven rectangular textile of Assam, India
blurb: The Gamosa of Assam is an article of significance for the people of Assam, India. It is generally a white rectangular piece of cloth with primarily a red border on three sides and red woven motifs on the fourth.

title: Garad sari
about: Traditional handwoven cotton sari of West Bengal
blurb: Garad sari is a traditional handwoven sari of West Bengal. It is produced in Murshidabad and Birbhum districts of West Bengal. Mrityunjay Sarkar, a weaver of Mirzapur, is the inventor of this famous sari.

title: Ghagra choli
about: Traditional clothing of women from the Indian subcontinent
blurb: Ghagra choli is a type of skirt and blouse pair of ethnic clothing for women from the Indian subcontinent, notably in the Indian states of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Haryana, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu and Kashmir and in the Terai plains of southern…

title: Gharara
about: Traditional outfit of the Indian subcontinent similar to a flared skirt
blurb: A gharara is a traditional Lucknowi outfit, traditionally worn by Muslim women of the Hindi-Urdu Belt region of India. It consists of a kurti, a dupatta, and most importantly, a pair of wide-legged pants, ruched at the knee so they flare out dramatically known as Gharara.

title: Goldwork
blurb: Goldwork is the art of embroidery using metal threads. It is particularly prized for the way light plays on it. The term "goldwork" is used even when the threads are imitation gold, silver, or copper.

title: Golf Wang
blurb: Golf Wang is an American street-wear brand established in 2011 by American musician Tyler, the Creator. The name Golf Wang is a spoonerism of his Los Angeles-based musical collective Odd Future Wolf Gang Kill Them All or Odd Future for short, of which he was a co-founder.

title: Gopalpur tussar silk
blurb: The village of Gopalpur in Jajpur District in the Indian state of Odisha is known for producing tussar silk. The handicraft received the Geographical Indication tag by the Government of India in 2009. The fabric may be used for dhoti, shawls, scarves, and saris.

title: Guess
blurb: Guess?, Inc. is an American clothing company, notable for its black-and-white advertisements. It licenses its brand on other fashion accessories, such as watches, jewelry, perfumes, bags and shoes. Operating in several countries around the world, most of its stores are in the USA and Canada.

title: Habaspuri sari
blurb: Habaspuri(Odia pronunciation: [habɔsɔpuɾi]) is a cotton-based traditional handloom textile of Odisha, India. The Habaspuri sari is a major handloom sari product of this textile.

title: Handloom sari
blurb: Handloom saris are a traditional textile art of Bangladesh and India. The production of handloom saris is important for economic development in rural India. Completion of a single sari takes two to three days of work.

title: Haudenosaunee clothing
about: Traditional and modern garments of the Haudenosaunee nations
blurb: Haudenosaunee clothing is the traditional and modern garments of the six Haudenosaunee nations. Haudenosaunee fashion has changed substantially since European colonization, shaped by both the introduction of new materials and the effects of colonial warfare and territorial dispossession.

title: Hollister Co.
blurb: Hollister Co., often advertised as Hollister or HCo., is a retail brand owned by Abercrombie & Fitch Co, selling apparel, accessories, and fragrances. Goods are available in-store and through the company's online store.

title: Ilkal sari
about: Form of saree originating from Ilkal, Bagalkot, Karnataka, India
blurb: Ilkal sari or Ilkal seere is a traditional form of sari which is a common feminine wear in India. Ilkal sari takes its name from the town of Ilkal in the Bagalkot district of Karnataka state, India.

title: Imogene + Willie
about: Blue jeans made in Nashville, Tennessee
blurb: Imogene + Willie set up shop in Nashville in 2009 on a quest to make the perfect pair of jeans, and makes them in the USA.

title: Inuit clothing
about: Traditional clothing of the indigenous peoples of Arctic North America
blurb: Traditional Inuit clothing is a complex system of cold-weather garments historically made from animal hide and fur, worn by Inuit, a group of culturally related Indigenous peoples inhabiting the Arctic areas of Canada, Greenland, and the United States.

title: Jamdani
blurb: Jamdani is a fine muslin textile produced for centuries in South Rupshi of Narayanganj district in Bangladesh on the bank of Shitalakshya River. The historic production of jamdani was patronized by imperial warrants of the Mughal emperors.

title: Jingle dress
about: Native American and First Nations dance
blurb: Jingle dress is a First Nations and Native American women's pow wow regalia and dance. North Central College associate professor Matthew Krystal notes, in his book, Indigenous Dance and Dancing Indian: Contested Representation in the Global Era, that "Whereas men's styles offer Grass Dance as a…

title: Jodhpuri
about: Type of suit popular in India
blurb: A Jodhpuri suit or bandhgala, is a formal suit from Rajasthan, India. It originated in the erstwhile princely Jodhpur State in former Rajputana and gained popularity in India during the mid-19th to mid-20th century. It consists of a coat and trousers, sometimes accompanied by a vest.

title: Kalamkari
blurb: Kalamkari, also commonly spelled as qalamkari, is an ancient textile printing art, that originated in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. Kalamkari gained popularity in the South India during the reign of Vijayanagara Empire.

title: Kanchipuram silk sari
about: Type of silk saree made in Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu, India
blurb: The Kanchipuram silk sari, also called Kanjeevaram sari is a type of silk sari made in the Kanchipuram region in Tamil Nadu, India. These saris are worn as bridal & special occasion saris by most women in Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka & Andhra Pradesh.

title: Kani Shawl
blurb: The Kani shawl is a type of Kashmiri shawl originating from the Kanihama area of the Kashmir Valley of Jammu and Kashmir, India. It is one of the oldest handicrafts of India's Kashmir. This craft has been a part of the valley since the time of Mughals. The shawls are woven from pashmina yarn.

title: Kantha
blurb: Kantha, also spelled kanta or qanta, is a type of embroidery craft in Bangladesh and eastern regions of India, particularly in the Indian states of West Bengal, Tripura and Odisha. In Odisha, old saris are stacked on each other and hand-stitched to make a thin piece of cushion.

title: Kasta sari
blurb: The Kaashtha sari is a Koli style of sari, draping in a similar way to the Maharashtrian dhoti. The word Kaashtha refers to the sari being tucked at the back. Since this sari is usually worn using a single nine yard cloth, it is also referred to as Nauvari, which means Nine Yards.

title: Kasuti
about: Traditional form of folk embroidery from Karnataka, India
blurb: Kasuti is a traditional form of folk embroidery practised in the state of Karnataka, India. Kasuti work which is very intricate sometimes involves putting up to 5,000 stitches by hand and is traditionally made on dresswear like Ilkal sarees, Ravike/Kuppasa and Angi.

title: Kemben
blurb: Kemben is a form of Native Indonesian torso wrap originally found in traditional native Java and Bali clothing cultures. It is made by wrapping a piece of kain, usually but not limited to batik, tenun, ikat, or any type of fabrics, covering the chest wrapped around one's torso.

title: Kerala sari
about: Sari type originating from Kerala, India
blurb: Kerala sari is a clothing of women in the Indian state of Kerala.

title: Khadi
about: Hand-spun cloth from the Indian subcontinent, usually made out of cotton
blurb: Khadi, derived from khaddar, is a hand-spun and woven natural fibre cloth. It was promoted by Mahatma Gandhi as swadeshi during India's freedom struggle, and the term is used throughout the Indian subcontinent.

title: Khalat
about: Traditional garment of Central and South Asia
blurb: A khalat is a loose, long-sleeved outer silk or cotton robe common in Central Asia and South Asia and worn both by men and women, although in differing styles.

title: Kith
blurb: Kith is an American fashion and lifestyle brand established in New York City in 2011 by Ronnie Fieg. The brand began as a footwear retailer, and later expanded to streetwear, fashion, and lifestyle.

title: Koorai silk sari
about: Textile industry in Tamil Nadu and Silk in India
blurb: 11°06′06″N 79°39′09″E / 11.101800°N 79.652600°E / 11.101800; 79.652600 Koorai silk sari, also referred to as Koorai pattu pudavai, Koorai pattu, or Koranad cloth, is a traditional nine-yard sari originating from Koranad in Mayiladuthurai, Tamil Nadu, India.

title: Kota Doria
blurb: Kota Doria or Kota Doriya is the name of a light woven fabric made of tiny woven squares which is still handwoven on traditional pit looms in Kaithoon near Kota in Rajasthan and in some of the surrounding villages.

title: Kurta
about: Loose shirt or tunic worn traditionally in South Asia
blurb: A kurta is a loose collarless shirt or tunic worn in many regions of South Asia, and now also worn around the world.

title: Kutch embroidery
about: Handicraft and textile art tradition of Kutch, Gujarat, India
blurb: Kutch embroidery is a handicraft and textile signature art tradition of the tribal community of Kutch district in Gujarat, India. The tradition and its designs has made a notable contribution to Indian embroidery traditions.

title: Lee
blurb: Lee is an American brand of jeans made from denim, first produced in 1889 in Salina, Kansas. The company is owned by Kontoor Brands, a spin-off of VF Corporation's Jeanswear Division. Since 2019 its headquarters has been in Greensboro, North Carolina, relocated from Merriam, Kansas.

title: Left Field NYC
about: Durable menswear made in the USA
blurb: Left Field NYC makes durable men's clothing, from denim jeans and uniform chinos to tees, cut and sewn in the USA.

title: Lehenga
about: Long, embroidered, pleated skirt of the Indian subcontinent
blurb: The lehenga, lehnga or langa is a form of ankle-length skirt from the Indian subcontinent. Different patterns and styles of traditional embroidery are used to decorate lehenga. Gota patti embroidery is often used for festivals and weddings.

title: Lehenga-style sari
about: Combination of sari and lehenga choli
blurb: A lehenga-style sari is a modern garment introduced in India that blends elements of the traditional sari and lehenga choli. A lehenga-style sari is normally 4.5 metres to 5.5 metres long. To wear one, unlike a sari, one does not have to form pleats but may simply tuck and drape.

title: Levi Strauss & Co.
blurb: Levi Strauss & Co. is an American clothing company known worldwide for its Levi's brand of denim jeans.

title: Levi's 501
blurb: The button-fly blue jean patented in the 1870s for miners, and the template for almost every pair of jeans since.

title: Louis Philippe
blurb: Louis Philippe is a premium brand of men's apparel originating from India. It is a subsidiary of Madura Fashion & Lifestyle.

title: Lungi
about: Men's skirt from the Indian subcontinent
blurb: The lungi is a men's skirt usually tied around the lower waist below the navel that originated in the Indian subcontinent.

title: Madapollam
blurb: Madapollam /ˌmædəˈpɒləm/ is a soft cotton fabric manufactured from fine yarns with a dense pick laid out in linen weave. Madapollam is used as an embroidery and handkerchief fabric and as a base for fabric printing.

title: Makuṭa
about: Headdress used as crown in Southeast Asia
blurb: The makuṭa, variously known in several languages as makuta, mahkota, magaik, mokot, mongkut or chada, is a type of headdress used as crowns in the Southeast Asian monarchies of today's Cambodia and Thailand, and historically in Indonesia, Malaysia, Sri Lanka, Laos and Myanmar.

title: Manila shawl
blurb: The Manila shawl is an embroidered silk shawl derived from the Philippine alampay or scarf. They were popular in the Philippines, Latin America, and Spain during the colonial era. It was also adopted and became popular in European fashions in the 19th century.

title: Manta
about: Textile worn as a blanket or wrap-around dress
blurb: A manta is a rectangular textile that was worn as a blanket or as a wrap-around dress. When worn as a dress, the manta is held together by a woven sash. Mantas are worn by such indigenous peoples as the Navajo, Hopi, and Pueblo peoples.

title: Matchcoat
about: Native American outer garment consisting of a length of coarse woolen cloth (stroud)
blurb: A matchcoat or match coat is an outer garment consisting of a length of coarse woolen cloth, usually about 2 yards long, worn wrapped around the upper part of the body like a toga.

title: Mekhela sador
blurb: Mekhela sador is traditional clothing worn by women from Assam. It is a two-piece outfit, consisting of the mekhela and the sador, and is generally made from Assam silk such as muga, eri or pat silk.

title: Mianfu
blurb: Mianfu is a kind of Chinese clothing in hanfu; it was worn by emperors, kings, and princes, and in some instances by the nobles in historical China from the Shang to the Ming dynasty.

title: Muga silk
blurb: Muga silk is a variety of wild silk geographically tagged to the state of Assam in India. The silk is known for its extreme durability and has a natural yellowish-golden tint with a shimmering, glossy texture.

title: Mundu
about: Traditional draped garment for the lower body, worn in South Asia and the Maldives
blurb: The mundu is a garment worn around the waist in the Indian states of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, the Lakshadweep archipelago, and the Indian Ocean island nation of Maldives. It is closely related to sarongs like dhotis and lungis. It is normally woven in cotton and coloured white or cream.

title: Mundum neriyatum
about: Traditional clothing of women in Kerala
blurb: Mundum neriyatum is the traditional clothing of women in Kerala, a state in southwestern India. It is the oldest remnant of the ancient form of the sari which covered only the lower part of the body.

title: Muslin
about: Cotton fabric of fine plain weave
blurb: Muslin is a cotton fabric of plain weave. It is made in a wide range of weights from delicate sheers to coarse sheeting. Muslin was produced in different regions of South Asia; the Bengal region was the main manufacturing area.

title: Mysore silk
about: Variety of mulberry silk produced in the Indian district of Mysore
blurb: Mysore silk is a variety of mulberry silk associated with Mysore, Karnataka, India. The silk industry in the Mysore region, which had declined after the fall of the Vijayanagara Empire, was revived during the reign of Tipu Sultan in the late 18th century.

title: Nakshi kantha
blurb: Nakshi kantha, a type of embroidered quilt, is a centuries-old Bengali art tradition of the Bengal region, notably in Bangladesh and the Indian states of West Bengal, Tripura, and parts of Assam. The basic materials used are thread and old cloth.

title: Nehru jacket
blurb: The Nehru jacket is a hip-length tailored coat for men or women, with a mandarin collar, and with its front modelled on the longer Indian achkan or sherwani frequently worn by Jawaharlal Nehru, the prime minister of India from 1947 to 1964.

title: Odisha Ikat
blurb: Odisha Ikat, is a kind of ikat known as Bandhakala and Bandha, a resist dyeing technique, originating from Indian state of Odisha. Traditionally known as "Bandhakala"', "Bandha", '"Bandha of Odisha", it is a geographically tagged product of Odisha since 2007.

title: Okhai
about: Hand-embroidered clothing by rural Indian artisans
blurb: Okhai sells handcrafted apparel and lifestyle pieces made by rural artisans from across India, from hand-embroidered kurtas to dresses.

title: OshKosh B'gosh
blurb: OshKosh B'gosh is an American children's apparel company founded in Oshkosh, Wisconsin. It is a subsidiary of Carter's. OshKosh B'gosh has become best known for its children's clothing, especially bibbed overalls.

title: Paithani
blurb: Paithani is a variety of sari, named after the Paithan in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district from the state of Maharashtra in India where the sari was first made by hand. Present day Yeola, a town in Nashik, Maharashtra is the largest manufacturer of Paithani.

title: Pashmina
blurb: Pashmina refers to, depending on the source, the cashmere wool of the Changthangi cashmere goat, or fine Kashmiri cashmere wool. The word pashm means "wool" in Persian, but in Kashmir, pashm referred to the raw unspun wool of domesticated Changthangi goats.

title: Pheran
blurb: Pheran or Phiran is the traditional outfit for both males and females in Kashmir. The pheran consists of two gowns, one over the other. The traditional pheran extends to the feet, which was popular up to the late 19th century C.E.

title: Phulkari
blurb: Phulkari is the folk embroidery of the Punjab region and Gulkari of Sindh in South Asia. It is an artwork traditionally created by women. Although phulkari means 'floral work', the designs include not only flowers but also cover motifs and geometrical shapes.

title: Pochampally sari
blurb: Pochampally sari or Pochampalli ikat is a saree made in Bhoodan Pochampally, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district, Telangana State, India. They have traditional geometric patterns in "Paagadu Bandhu" style of dyeing. The intricate geometric designs find their way into sarees and dress materials.

title: Prairie dress
about: Skirt with one or more deep flounces, loosely inspired by 1830s styles
blurb: A prairie dress or prairie skirt is a modest American style of skirt, an article of women's and girls' clothing. Prairie dresses may be straight to slightly flared to very full, and may have one or more flounces or tiers; prairie dresses may be worn over a ruffled eyelet or lace-trimmed petticoat.

title: Punjabi tamba and kurta
about: Type of sarong and shirt, traditional costume in Punjab
blurb: Punjabi Kurta and Tamba are traditional costume for men of Punjab.

title: Qaba
blurb: A qaba is a long coat with sleeves and buttons, similar to a cassock, open at the front. The Mughal emperors wore ankle-length garments. The outfits during the reign of Babur and Humayun are more or less the same, i.e. qaba, jama, pirahan, jilucha, jiba and kasaba.

title: Ralph Lauren Corporation
blurb: Ralph Lauren Corporation is a publicly traded American fashion and lifestyle brand founded in 1967 by American businessman Ralph Lauren in New York City. The company markets products in apparel, home, accessories, and fragrances, and is most known for its flagship brand, Polo Ralph Lauren.

title: Raw Mango
about: Saris and garments drawn from Indian cultures
blurb: Raw Mango makes saris and garments that draw on the colours, philosophies and cultures of India.

title: Raymond Group
blurb: Raymond Group is an Indian branded fabric and fashion retailer, incorporated in 1925. It produces suiting fabric, with a capacity of producing 31 million meters of wool and wool-blended fabrics.

title: Roach
blurb: Porcupine hair roaches are a traditional male headdress of a number of Native American tribes in what is now New England, the Great Lakes and Missouri River regions, including the Potawatomi who lived where Chicago now stands.

title: Sadri
about: Vest-jacket worn by men in South Asia
blurb: Sadri, also known as a Waskat or Bandi, is a vest-jacket worn by men in South Asia, while women sometimes wear a similar waistcoat known as a Koti. In Europe and America, the sadri became known as a Nehru vest.

title: Salwar
about: Traditional loose trousers worn in South Asia
blurb: Salwar or shalwar is cloth worn from the waist to the ankles, covering both legs separately. It is the lower-garment of the shalwar kameez suit which is widely-worn in South Asia. It is known for its lively hues, rich fabrics, and embroidery.

title: Sambalpuri sari
blurb: A Sambalpuri sari is a traditional handwoven bandha sari wherein the warp and the weft are tie-dyed before weaving. It is a handloom sari produced in the Sambalpur, Bargarh, Balangir, Boudh and Sonepur districts of Odisha, India.

title: Sari
about: Woman's draped garment of the Indian subcontinent
blurb: A sari is a draped cloth and women's garment in the Indian subcontinent. It consists of an un-stitched stretch of woven fabric arranged over the body as a dress, with one end attached to the waist, while the other end rests over one shoulder as a stole, sometimes baring a part of the midriff.

title: Seersucker
blurb: Seersucker, hickory stripe or railroad stripe is a thin, puckered, cotton fabric, usually striped or chequered, used to make clothing for hot weather.

title: Shalwar kameez
about: Trousers and tunic worn in South Asia
blurb: Shalwar kameez is a traditional combination dress worn by men and women in South Asia, and Central Asia. Shalwars are trousers which are atypically wide at the waist and narrow to a cuffed bottom.

title: Skims
about: American fashion company founded by Kim Kardashian and Jens Grede
blurb: SKIMS is an American shapewear and clothing brand co-founded by Kim Kardashian and Jens Grede. The business was valued at over $5 billion as of 2025[update].

title: Stetson
blurb: Stetson is an American brand of hat manufactured by the John B. Stetson Company. John B. Stetson gained inspiration for his most famous hats when he headed west from his native New Jersey for health reasons. On his return east in 1865, he founded the John B. Stetson Company in Philadelphia.

title: Summit Ice Apparel
blurb: Summit Ice Apparel is a not-for-profit apparel company founded by comedian Nathan Fielder. Fielder started the company in 2015, in response to Vancouver-based company Taiga posting a tribute to Holocaust denier Doug Collins.

title: Supreme
blurb: Supreme is an American clothing brand established in Manhattan, New York City, in April 1994. The company focuses on streetwear, skateboarding, and hip-hop fashion trends. Supreme has been described as one of the most influential streetwear brands globally.

title: Tear dress
blurb: A tear dress is a long dress made of calico worn by Oklahoma Cherokee women. The tear dress is the official dress of the Cherokee Nation.

title: Tellason
about: Raw selvedge denim cut and sewn in San Francisco
blurb: Tellason has made raw selvedge denim jeans and jackets in San Francisco since 2009: classic American workwear built to last and to fade well.

title: Toda Embroidery
about: Embroidery of the Toda pastoral people of Nilgiris, in Tamil Nadu
blurb: Toda embroidery, also locally known as "pukhoor", is an art work among the Toda pastoral people of Nilgiris, in Tamil Nadu, made exclusively by their women.

title: Toghu
blurb: Toghu, or atoghu, is a traditional royal garment of the Grassfields peoples of the Northwest and West regions of Cameroon, made of black velvet embroidered with brightly coloured patterns.

title: Tom Ford
blurb: Tom Ford SA is an American luxury fashion house founded by namesake designer Tom Ford in 2005. Its product line features ready-to-wear and made-to-measure offerings, as well as footwear, accessories, handbags, cosmetics and fragrances.

title: Tommy Hilfiger
blurb: Tommy Hilfiger B.V., formerly known as Tommy Hilfiger Corporation and Tommy Hilfiger Inc., is a Dutch-based American clothing brand that manufactures apparel and licensed products such as footwear, accessories, fragrances and home furnishings.

title: Traje de flamenca
about: Traditional clothing of flamenco dancers of Andalusia
blurb: The traje de flamenca or traje de gitana is the dress traditionally worn by women at Ferias in Andalusia, Spain. There are two forms: one worn by dancers and the other worn as a day dress. The day dress is body-hugging to mid-thigh, and then continues in multiple layers of ruffles to the ankle.

title: Tussar silk
about: Coarse silk from wild Antheraea silkworms
blurb: Tussar silk is a type of wild silk, produced from the larvae of Antheraea silkworms, including A. assamensis, A. paphia, A. pernyi, A. roylei, and A. yamamai.

title: Under Armour
about: American sports clothing and accessories company
blurb: Under Armour, Inc. is an American sportswear company that manufactures footwear and apparel headquartered in Baltimore, Maryland, United States.

title: Uttariya
about: Upper body garment of Vedic period
blurb: An uttariya is a loose piece of upper body clothing with its origins in ancient India. It is a single piece of cloth that falls from the back of the neck to curl around both arms and could also drape the top half of the body. An uttariya is similar to a veil, a long scarf and shawl.

title: Volcom
blurb: Volcom is an American lifestyle brand that designed, marketed, and distributed boardsports-oriented products. Volcom is headquartered in Costa Mesa, California. The brand was known for its trademark stone logo, its slogan True to This, and the Let the Kids Ride Free campaign.

title: Yupʼik clothing
about: Traditional clothing worn by the Yup'ik people of Alaska
blurb: Yup'ik clothing refers to the traditional Alaska Native-style clothing worn by the Yupik people of southwestern Alaska. The traditional clothing systems developed and used by the Yup’ik, Inuit and Nuniwarmiut peoples performs similarly to the most effective cold weather clothing developed to date.
